hero.headline: The No-Village C-Section
hero.subheadline: First 14 Days Alone With a Newborn After Major Abdominal Surgery - Survival & Function
hero.body: Recovering from major abdominal surgery while solely carrying newborn care - lifting rules, pain schedule, incision checks, feeding round the clock - alone. She does not know what is safe to do, how to manage pain and movement solo, what normal healing looks like versus infection, and collapses under the load by day 4. A day-by-day solo recovery system - pain on schedule, safe movement, incision watch, minimum-viable household - plus red flags that end guesswork.
hero.trust_line: Educational content - not medical advice. Your clinician overrides everything here.
hero.evidence_label: Educational content informed by sourced research and clinical guidance. It is not a substitute for medical, clinical, or mental-health assessment.

before_state.label: Sound familiar?
paragraphs: Right now pushing through pain, lifting toddler/laundry too early, skipping meds to 'stay clear-headed', and lying frozen in bed fearing movement - and the people who matter most (mother, partner (part-time), and distant relatives by phone) are all pulling in different directions.
On top of that, unmanaged pain-sleep spiral, household load unchanged, and no incision surveillance.
It feels like overwhelm, guilt about rest, and fear of the wound.
The cost: slower healing, wound stress, and breakdown around day 4.
before_state.punch: This is not a personal failing. It is a system gap - and The No-Village C-Section closes it.

items.title: The No-Village 14-Day Guide
items.description: You came home from a C-section without a mother, auntie, or cousin installed in your guest room. Maybe your partner got two weeks off, maybe five days, maybe none. Everyone online

items.title: The Incision Decision Card
items.description: Beyond two weeks of weepy blues -> or any moment of "I can't do this," hopelessness, thoughts of harming yourself or the baby -> this is medical, not moral. Contact your clinician

items.title: Bad-Day Rescue Card + crisis lines
items.description: A bad day is not a failed recovery. Surgical healing is not linear. Today we drop to MINIMUM MODE and tomorrow restarts - no debt, no guilt.

for_items: Woman in the first two weeks after a C-section, home without nearby family support ('no village'), often with a partner back at work within days
Recovering from major abdominal surgery while solely carrying newborn care - lifting rules, pain schedule, incision checks, feeding round the clock - alone
Tried to run the pre-baby household at pre-baby speed; paid for it with agony and tears - or lay frozen in bed afraid to move at all
who_for.not_for_label: This is NOT for you if
not_for_items: Coordinates solo recovery logistics ONLY. Never diagnoses infection/clots/depression, never adjusts prescriptions, never replaces the week-2 visit or 6-week clearance.
If any red flag is present (fever >=38C/chills; spreading incision redness/swelling/opening/pus/foul fluid; worsening pain after day 3-4), this is not a home system - seek professional care first.

promise.label: What we promise - and what we don't
promise.we_do: A day-by-day solo recovery system - pain on schedule, safe movement, incision watch, minimum-viable household - plus red flags that end guesswork. A day-by-day survival-and-function plan she can execute ALONE: pain on schedule, safe movement, clean incision watch, minimum-viable household - and clear red flags that end guesswork.
promise.we_do_not: We do not promise: full recovery still ~6 weeks, cannot self-diagnose complications, and some days will simply be hard. This is an educational system, not medical, clinical, or mental-health care.
promise.evidence_label: Educational content informed by sourced research and clinical guidance. It is not a substitute for medical, clinical, or mental-health assessment.
